public_rationale: The required trigger is not established. The Andersen records concern ongoing proceedings, while the Anthropic settlement does not establish a plaintiff victory holding model training unlawful. Its rejection of model-deletion requests matters under a broader reading of 'prevail', but does not justify scoring the narrower conditional forecast. Neither procedural progress nor a settlement payment demonstrates the predicted retraining costs and capability losses.
limitations: The lawsuit scope and meaning of 'prevail' materially affect the assessment.
The latest Andersen status is supplemented by a secondary tracker rather than a complete certified docket.
Unknown accounting basis independently prevents a supported or contradicted finding on the cost component.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If any of these copyright lawsuits prevail, it would be calamitous for OpenAI and Anthropic and even more so for Google and Meta, mostly because models can't practically forget training data and would need costly retraining from scratch that would cost billions and dramatically reduce their efficacy.
conditions: if any of these lawsuits prevail

statement.excerpt: If any of these lawsuits prevail, it would be calamitous for OpenAI and Anthropic, and even more so for Google and Meta, whose Gemini and Llama models use datasets including millions of artists' work, mostly because it's "virtually impossible" for AI models to forget training data, meaning that they'd need to be retrained from scratch, which would cost billions of dollars and dramatically reduce their efficacy at tasks they're already not particularly good at.

from_speaker: If any of these lawsuits prevail
even more so for Google and Meta
our_interpretation: The preceding discussion makes a plaintiff victory establishing copyright liability for model training the relevant trigger. Surviving dismissal is insufficient.
The nearest referent is the litigation involving Stability AI, DeviantArt and Midjourney. Whether the phrase also includes every copyright case mentioned in the post is unclear.
A settlement concerning acquisition of pirated books does not automatically establish the stated training-liability trigger.
The practical prediction requires evidence of mandatory complete retraining, its cost, and substantial capability losses. A financial penalty alone does not establish that chain.
criteria.support_condition: A qualifying plaintiff victory leads to mandatory retraining from scratch, documented multibillion-dollar retraining costs, substantial capability losses, and the claimed severe consequences for the named developers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a qualifying victory, a final remedy and documented implementation establish that the affected models can continue operating without the predicted complete retraining and capability losses.
